newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African alcohol duties rise seen hitting revenue.
newsitem.headline: S.African alcohol duties rise seen hitting revenue.

text.p: The steep increases in excise duties on alcohol announced by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel this week could encourage smuggling and illegal trading, a leading retailer warned on Friday.
It could also dampen sales and the combined effect would be to decrease expected revenue levels, Picardi Rebel marking director Darron Swersky said. The store is part of the Rebhold group.
He said that while excise duty increases had been expected, he was concerned that the government had not given any indication of reallocating revenues to alleviate problems facing the industry.
These included illegal trading, smuggling and excise avoidance.
"It is unfortunate that the government is not visibly redirecting funds to support the liquor industry (and solve these problems)," Swersky said.
